newsitem.title: FRANCE: Three bombs kill one, wound 42 in Algiers - officials.
newsitem.headline: Three bombs kill one, wound 42 in Algiers - officials.

text.p: Three bombs exploded on Sunday in Algiers killing one person and wounding 42 others, Algerian security forces said.
A car bomb exploded near Algiers' law university in Ben Aknoun district killing one and wounding 12, they said in a statement read on the Algerian state-run radio.
Fifteen minutes earlier, another car bomb went off some hundreds metres (yards) away in the same district wounding nine people, the statement said.
Another bomb went off one hour before near a disco in a park, some two kilometres (1.25 miles) away in the same district, wounding 21 people, the statement added.
The bombings came five days after a bomb explosion killed three schoolgirls and a 12-year-old boy outside a high school in central Algiers.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algerian violence since early 1992 when authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
